questions.q: A radio station in Accra, Ghana (located on longitude $0^\circ$) broadcasts a live sports event at $14:00$ GMT. At what local time will a listener in a town located at longitude $45^\circ\text{E}$ receive the live broadcast?
questions.explain:
To calculate local time based on longitude, we use the principle that the Earth rotates $15^\circ$ every $1$ hour (or $1^\circ$ every $4$ minutes).

**Step 1:** Calculate the longitudinal difference.
$$\text{Difference} = 45^\circ - 0^\circ = 45^\circ$$

**Step 2:** Convert the difference to time.
$$45^\circ \times 4 \text{ minutes} = 180 \text{ minutes} = 3 \text{ hours}$$

**Step 3:** Add or subtract the time based on direction. Places to the East are ahead in time (add), while places to the West are behind (subtract).
Since the town is $45^\circ$ **East** of Accra, we add the time difference:
$$14:00 + 3 \text{ hours} = 17:00 \text{ hours}$$

questions.q: The Earth undergoes both rotation and revolution. Which of the following natural phenomena is primarily caused by the Earth's **revolution** around the Sun, rather than its rotation on its axis?
options: The daily occurrence of day and night
The deflection of planetary winds and ocean currents
The varying lengths of day and night throughout the year
The daily rise and fall of ocean tides
questions.explain:
The Earth's **revolution** (its orbit around the Sun), combined with the tilt of its axis at $23.5^\circ$, is responsible for the changing seasons, the varying altitudes of the midday sun, and the **varying lengths of day and night** at different times of the year. 

Options A, B, and D (occurrence of day/night, deflection by the Coriolis force, and tides) are all direct consequences of the Earth's **rotation** on its own axis every 24 hours.

questions.q: The internal structure of the Earth is divided into concentric layers. The innermost layer, known as the core or barysphere, is characterized by very high temperatures and pressures. Which two chemical elements predominantly make up this layer?
questions.explain:
The Earth's core is mainly composed of heavy metals, specifically **Nickel (Ni)** and **Iron (Fe)**, which is why it is often referred to as **Nife**. 

By contrast, the outer continental crust is composed largely of silica and aluminum (**Sial**), and the oceanic crust and upper mantle are predominantly silica and magnesium (**Sima**).
